title: Hadacol crowds and stadium audiences
summary: How box tops gave admission, drawing 40-50 thousand people in stadiums, yet expenses were too great.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And that was the end of the Hattie call. It was a good idea while it lasted. Oh, he had a money.

Yeah. Well, do you know how many people we used to play there at one time? No. $50,000. Really? Yes. Where'd they do it? The admission to the shows, you had to have a box top of Hattie call. Yeah. Now, I think the Hattie call sold for a dollar and a half up to $3. So, either one, if you had a dollar and a half box or a $3 box, that was your admission. Yeah. And 40 and 50 thousand people. Now, you figure that out.
That was a lot of money.
Yeah, it was good profit in that medicine. Right.
But his expenses was too great. Yeah.

Where did you play? In the outdoors and stadiums? Well, you see, to accommodate people like that, 40, 50 thousand people, we played in football stadiums, in baseball parks, in all big places like that. Because you could never get that many people in a theater or an auditorium.
At that time, they didn't have auditoriums that big. No. No.
